info.name: Preservica - selected metadata for all assets (CSV)
info.description:
# Selected metadata for all assets in every top-level folder, as a CSV

Uses Preservica's search (the Content API, the same one the scheduled GitHub export uses) to pull the fields you choose for **every asset in every top-level folder**, a page at a time, then builds a CSV. The second column, `top_level_folder`, names the top-level folder each asset is in, so you can sort or filter by it in Excel.

**Before you start:** on this collection's **Variables** tab:
- fill in `username` and `password` in the **Current value** column;
- set `fields` to the fields you want, separated by commas (any names from `indexed_fields.csv` in the Scripts repository, e.g. `mods.title,mods.dateCreated,xip.security_descriptor`);
- leave `folderRefs` blank to cover all top-level folders. To cover only some, list their references separated by commas (request 2 shows them in the Console);
- click **Save**.

## Steps

1. Click the collection's **⋯** menu > **Run collection**, keep all five requests ticked, and click **Run**.
2. The run logs in, lists the top-level folders, counts the matching assets, and collects them 100 at a time. The **Console** shows progress, e.g. `Collected 300 of 1250`. It logs in again by itself if the token nears its 15-minute limit.
3. When the run finishes, open *5. Show the results as a CSV* and click the **Visualize** tab of its response. It shows the first 200 rows as a table, a **Download CSV** button, and the full CSV in a box. If the button doesn't download anything, click in the box, select all, copy, and paste into a new file saved with a `.csv` ending.

The CSV opens in Excel. Fields with several values (such as subjects) are joined with ` | `. Assets stored at the top level, outside any folder, have `top_level_folder` blank.

## Notes

- Only **indexed** fields can be returned; `indexed_fields.csv` lists them. To get every field of every record as XML, use the *download all metadata (export packages)* collection instead.
- Running the collection again clears the previous results and starts over.
- For tens of thousands of assets Postman can become slow; the GitHub export (`preservica_search_export.py`) handles that size better.
- 0 assets: check `folderRefs`, and that the account has **Read Metadata** on the records' security tags.

request.description: `POST /api/accesstoken/login`. Checks the username, password and tenant, and saves the token. Every later request sends it in the `Preservica-Access-Token` header and logs in again by itself when it's about to expire.

exec: // First page, or the next page when the list is longer than 100.
if (pm.response.code !== 200) { console.log(`Listing failed (HTTP ${pm.response.code}): ` + pm.response.text().slice(0, 300)); next(null); return; }
const a = {}; for (const x of m[1].matchAll(/(\w+)="([^"]*)"/g)) a[x[1]] = unescape(x[2]);
top.push({ type: a.type, ref: a.ref, title: a.title });
console.log(`Listed ${top.length} so far; fetching the next page.`);
// Fresh start: remember folder names for the CSV, and clear earlier results.
const names = {}; top.filter(t => t.type === 'SO').forEach(t => names[t.ref] = t.title);
const folders = top.filter(t => t.type === 'SO'), assets = top.filter(t => t.type === 'IO');
if (assets.length) console.log(`Plus ${assets.length} asset(s) stored directly at the top level, not in a folder.`);
console.log(top.length ? `${folders.length} top-level folder(s).` : 'Nothing is visible to this account: it needs Read Metadata on the records\' security tags.');

request.description: Lists every top-level folder (and any assets stored at the top level), following page links if there are more than 100. The Console shows each folder's title and reference.

exec: // Builds the search request from the collection variables.
const fields = pm.collectionVariables.get('fields').split(',').map(f => f.trim()).filter(f => f && f !== 'xip.reference' && f !== 'xip.top_level_so');
const filters = [{ name: 'xip.document_type', values: ['IO'] }];   // assets only
['xip.top_level_so'].concat(fields).forEach(f => filters.push({ name: f, values: [] }));   // return these fields
const body = [ { key: 'start', value: String(START) }, { key: 'max', value: String(MAX) },
{ key: 'q', value: JSON.stringify({ q: '%', fields: filters }) },
if (pm.response.code !== 200) { console.log(`Search failed (HTTP ${pm.response.code}): ` + pm.response.text().slice(0, 500)); next(null); return; }
console.log(`${total} asset(s) ${folders.length ? 'in the ' + folders.length + ' chosen folder(s)' : 'across all top-level folders'}. Collecting them now.`);

request.description: Counts the assets that match (all top-level folders, or those in `folderRefs`) and clears earlier results. The request body is filled in automatically from the `fields` and `folderRefs` variables.
